QL-006.theme: Fairness is worth more than winning

word.meaning: Giving people their rights and judging honestly, even when you prefer one side.

scenes.title: A ball on the boundary
scenes.alt: Umar and his friends inspect a cricket ball touching the boundary line.
scenes.text: The red ball rolled across the grass and stopped against the boundary. Umar was keeping score. Both teams waited for his decision.
scenes.speaker: Umar
scenes.dialogue: Let's check where it touched the line.

scenes.title: A friend asks for a favour
scenes.alt: Umar holds his scorebook while his friend asks him to change the score.
scenes.text: His best friend leaned closer. If Umar counted fewer runs for the other team, his own side might win. Umar liked his friend, but the rule had not changed.
scenes.speaker: His friend
scenes.dialogue: Could you count fewer runs—just this once?

scenes.title: A score everyone can trust
scenes.alt: Umar records the correct score while children from both teams watch.
scenes.text: Umar applied the agreed boundary rule and wrote the correct runs. His team did not gain an unfair advantage. The game could continue with an honest score.
scenes.speaker: Umar
scenes.dialogue: I am your friend. I still need to use the same rule for both teams.

decision.question: You are holding Umar's scorebook. What should you do?

choices.text: Count fewer runs because he is my best friend.
choices.feedback: Friendship does not change another team's rights. A fair scorer uses the same rule for both sides.

choices.text: Check the agreed rule and record the correct runs.
choices.feedback: Yes. Check the facts, use the same rule and explain your decision calmly. Being fair can cost your team an advantage.

choices.text: Let the loudest player decide so the argument stops.
choices.feedback: The loudest person is not always right. Check what happened and use the rule; ask an adult if the disagreement cannot be settled safely.

sequence: Apply the same agreed rule to everyone.
QL-006.mission: During a game or shared activity today, use the same rule for a friend and someone else.
QL-006.talk: Would your decision change if the teams swapped places? Explain why.
QL-006.remember: A friend deserves kindness. Everyone deserves fairness.

QL-007.theme: A promise becomes real through your actions

word.meaning: Being someone others can rely on to care for what is entrusted to them and follow through honestly.

scenes.title: A book and a promise
scenes.alt: Amina lends a coral storybook to Hana at the classroom bookshelf.
scenes.text: On Monday, Amina lent Hana a favourite storybook. They agreed that Hana would return it on Friday. Hana accepted the book carefully.
scenes.speaker: Hana
scenes.dialogue: Thank you. I will bring it back on Friday, inshaAllah.

scenes.title: One more chapter?
scenes.alt: Hana considers the unfinished borrowed book beside her schoolbag on Thursday evening.
scenes.text: On Thursday evening, Hana reached an exciting chapter. She wanted another day. Then she remembered that the book belonged to Amina, who was expecting it back.
scenes.speaker: Hana's thought
scenes.dialogue: I want to finish—but I agreed to return it tomorrow.

scenes.title: Trust goes back with the book
scenes.alt: Hana returns the borrowed storybook to Amina the following school morning.
scenes.text: Hana packed the book that evening and returned it on Friday. She asked whether she could borrow it again another time. Keeping her word mattered more than finishing immediately.
scenes.speaker: Hana
scenes.dialogue: Here is your book, as promised. May I borrow it again another time?

decision.question: What would help Hana keep her promise?

choices.text: Keep the book until I finish. Amina probably will not mind.
choices.feedback: That changes the agreement without Amina's permission. Return it on time, or ask before changing the plan.

choices.text: Tell Amina I returned it, even though it is still at home.
choices.feedback: A second wrong does not fix a missed promise. Be honest about what happened and arrange to put it right.

choices.text: Pack it tonight and return it on the agreed day.
choices.feedback: Yes. Planning makes a promise easier to keep. If an unavoidable problem prevents it, tell Amina promptly, apologise and ask about a new arrangement.

sequence: Agree honestly on what you can do and when.
Make a plan and prepare a reminder.
Follow through; communicate promptly if something unavoidable changes.
QL-007.mission: Choose one small commitment you can keep today. Say what you will do and when, then follow through.
QL-007.talk: What should Hana do if she becomes ill and cannot come to school on Friday?
QL-007.remember: Promise thoughtfully. Prepare carefully. Follow through honestly.
